paras: The Atlanta Christmas police shooting was the wounding of an unnamed Black man by an Atlanta policeman, who shot him in the leg on Christmas Day, 1882. The only reason given was that the man had tried to take the officer's club, and the shooting reached northern papers as one line in a wire list of Atlanta's Christmas "casualties."

According to the Atlanta despatch, the day was fair and "everybody was out," and the station houses booked 125 cases in ten hours. A correspondent for the Cincinnati Commercial wrote that apart from newspaper men the town had been "on a unanimous drunk."

The despatch reported that "a policeman shot a negro in the leg for attempting to take a club from him." The Commercial's version said the man was shot "through the leg" for trying to take "his club," meaning the officer's own. Neither the man nor the officer was named, and the account of the struggle comes only from the despatch, with no version from the wounded man.

The same list reported that another policeman was shot through his coat and trousers by an unknown person, that a drunk officer nearly started a riot by pushing a citizen, and that two Black prisoners fought bloodily in a cell. The Commercial's correspondent wrote that a policeman urged the prisoners on while two police commissioners stood by.
No report of an arrest, inquiry or charge against the officer appears in the coverage.

The despatch ran in northern papers from December 27 to 29, among them the Kennebec Journal, the Wilmington Daily Republican, the Vermont Phoenix and the Wilmington Daily Gazette. Editors used it as a picture of Southern holiday disorder, under headings such as "The Way They Celebrate Christmas in Georgia" and "Christmas-Day at the South—Some Incidents Not Down in the Northern Programme." The Wilmington Daily Republican printed it after a New Orleans account of a "disorderly and disgraceful" Christmas.

The Burlington Free Press quoted the list to answer a Boston Post claim that Vermont's crime record was worse than any Southern state's. The Commercial's correspondent called the cell fight disgraceful to the police and commissioners, but no paper questioned the stated reason for the shooting. Coverage of the shooting comes only from white papers.
The versions differ only in the despatch dateline, December 25 or 26, and in whether the club was described as the officer's.

accounts.label: Atlanta dispatch to the Cincinnati Commercial
accounts.gist: Same list in nearly the same words, saying the man tried to take 'his club' and adding criticism of the police and commissioners over a drunk officer and a cell fight.

framing.detail: The Kennebec Journal headed the despatch 'The Way They Celebrate Christmas in Georgia', presenting the shooting as part of Southern holiday disorder rather than as a police matter.
The Commercial's correspondent called the town 'on a unanimous drunk' and called the cell fight 'disgraceful' to police and commissioners, but repeated the shooting's stated reason without comment.
The Burlington Free Press quoted the casualty list to rebut a Boston Post claim about crime in Vermont.

conflicts.note: Only the dateline differs; both place the shooting on Christmas Day.
The Commercial version makes explicit that the club was the officer's.
